mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week recovery in RETAIL_REC (from -60.4% to -50.7% over three weeks) indicates a monotonic reopening trajectory. This trend will continue linearly, producing positive net change in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 9.7 percentage points over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines week-on-week at any point in the next four weeks, or the mean of RETAIL_REC over weeks t+1 to t+4 is lower than the mean over t-3w to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 19.4% to 16.0% over three weeks) signals residents spending more time outside homes. This behavioral shift drives increased RETAIL_REC visits as people resume out-of-home consumption patterns over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 17% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 3.4 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility stabilizes or increases while RETAIL_REC remains below -45%, indicating residents are not translating reduced home time into retail visits.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES recovery (from -49.3% to -45.3% over three weeks) combined with TRANSIT recovery (from -60.0% to -55.1%) indicates commuting infrastructure is normalizing. This dual recovery enables retail foot traffic to increase over the next four weeks as workers resume in-person routines and incidental shopping.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show consistent week-on-week improvement
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT reverses direction (declines week-on-week) while RETAIL_REC fails to reach -40%, indicating the commuting-retail linkage has broken.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains elevated (40.3% at t-0w) despite recent decline from 55.3%, signaling outdoor-activity preference persists. If PARKS stays above 35% over the next week, policy will remain permissive toward outdoor retail (markets, patios), sustaining RETAIL_REC above -50%.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 35% in the next week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at 40.3% at t-0w, well above baseline
failure_condition: PARKS drops below 25% in the next week while RETAIL_REC remains below -55%, indicating outdoor-activity restrictions have tightened without compensating indoor retail recovery.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near -17% (showing minimal week-on-week change from t-2w to t-0w), indicating essential-shopping patterns are locked in. This stability frees behavioral bandwidth for discretionary RETAIL_REC visits, which will increase over the next two weeks as consumers shift from essential-only to mixed shopping.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM variance week-on-week is less than 1 percentage point
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged only -15.4% to -17.4% across three weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM drops below -20% in the next two weeks, indicating renewed supply-chain or safety concerns that would suppress all retail mobility including discretionary categories.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July timing (t-0w = 2020-07-15) coincides with summer peak leisure season in Northern Hemisphere. Seasonal demand for outdoor and entertainment retail will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks independent of pandemic restrictions, as consumers pursue vacation-related shopping.
evidence_refs: fact:decision point is mid-July 2020, peak summer season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines below -55% in any week of the next four weeks, or the four-week mean is lower than the prior four-week mean, indicating seasonal demand is insufficient to overcome pandemic suppression.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility recovery (4.9 percentage point improvement from t-3w to t-0w) combined with WORKPLACES recovery (4.0 percentage point improvement) creates a multiplier effect: improved commuting access enables both workplace return and incidental retail visits. Over the next four weeks, this dual recovery will push RETAIL_REC above -45%.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:all three series show consistent improvement trajectory
failure_condition: TRANSIT or WORKPLACES reverses (declines week-on-week) in the next two weeks while RETAIL_REC remains below -48%, indicating the commuting-retail multiplier has decoupled.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with rising PARKS mobility indicates a behavioral shift toward outdoor activities. If this pattern persists (RESIDENTIAL < 17% AND PARKS > 35% simultaneously), consumers will substitute indoor retail with outdoor recreation, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 17% AND PARKS remains above 35% in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 16.0% and PARKS at 40.3% at t-0w show inverse pattern
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above -45% over the next two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining below 17% and PARKS above 35%, indicating outdoor-activity preference does not suppress indoor retail.
